the usage of context and content-based trust can improve the overall trust quality of a Semantic Web-based trust architecture and that the combination of reputation, context and content-based mechanisms allows the formulation of flexible, fine-granular trust policies for specific application domains.

(1) the current discussion about future trust architectures is focused on reputations and ratings and does not consider other types of trust relevant data, and (2) the combination of reputational and context- and contentbased trust mechanisms is a promising way to formulate subjective trust policies.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

trust policies on the Semantic Web can be defined as a combination of different trust mechanisms and that the usage of these policies can be used to support trust decisions in a wide variety of application scenarios.
we show how to use trust policies to define and evaluate the trust of a service provider in the Semantic Web.
the proposed trust architecture allows the formulation of trust policies as a weighted combination of trust ratings, context- and content information.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, besides of reputation-based trust mechanisms, context and content-based trust evaluation mechanisms should be integrated into a trust architecture for the Semantic Web.
, in order to be useful for real world applications, trust mechanisms have to be flexible and task- and application-specific.

trust policies on the Semantic Web can be formulated in a more flexible, fine-grain and task-specific way, which allows the usage of a wide range of application-specific data for the trust evaluation.
